questions.prompt: Name a name the Qur'an gives to Hell.

notAccepted.message: That isn't a name for Hell itself. Try again!

answers.explanation: The most common name for Hell in the Qur'an.
'The Fire', whose fuel is people and stones.
The Blazing Fire.
The Blaze.
"And what will make you know what Saqar is? It leaves nothing and spares nothing."

A raging flame that strips away the skin.
The Abyss — the home of those whose scales are light.
The Home of Ruin.

questions.prompt: Name a name or description the Qur'an gives to itself.

answers.explanation: 'The Recitation' — its best-known name.
'The Book', in which there is no doubt.
'The Criterion' between right and wrong; Surah 25 is named after it.
'The Reminder', which Allah Himself preserves.
Guidance for those who are mindful of Allah.
A clear light sent down.
The Word of Allah.
'The Revelation' sent down by the Lord of the worlds.
A healing for what is in the hearts.
A mercy for the believers.
A clear explanation for people.
'The Clear Book'.
An admonition from your Lord.
A conclusive proof from your Lord.
'The Wise' — "By the Qur'an, full of wisdom."
'The Glorious' — "Qaf. By the glorious Qur'an."
'The Noble' — "It is a noble Qur'an."
'The Mighty' — "it is a mighty Book."
'The best of statements'.
'Oft-repeated' — a Book consistent and repeated.
'The rope of Allah' to hold fast to, which many explain as the Qur'an.
answers.note: Commentators also explain the rope as Islam or the community.

questions.prompt: Name a part or feature of a mosque.

answers.explanation: The tower from which the call to prayer is given.
The great rounded roof over many prayer halls.
The niche in the wall that shows the direction of the qiblah.
The pulpit for the Friday sermon — the Prophet's ﷺ was three steps high.
The main covered space where the congregation prays.
The open court, or sahn, before the prayer hall.
Where worshippers wash before prayer.
Carpets, often marked in rows, that cover the floor.
The wall facing Makkah, where the mihrab is set.
Rows of arches, such as the horseshoe arches of Cordoba.
Qur'anic verses written across walls and domes.
A space or gallery set aside for women.
Honeycomb-like vaulting in domes and niches.
A vaulted hall walled on three sides and open on the fourth.
A carved wooden lattice screen.
A raised platform from which a caller repeats the imam's words.
A folding wooden stand (rehal) to hold the Qur'an.
